page: Microsoft Azure D16ads_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dadv6 server family, powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V74 processor with 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The memory configuration consists of 64.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is bundled, featuring a 945 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

Benchmark evaluations show strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores ranking in the top 25%. Text processing and text generation for small LLM models also demonstrate strong performance. However, multi-core performance, database operations, and memory write bandwidth fall into the average range. A notable performance tradeoff is observed in large-block read-only memory bandwidth, which is weak, and large-model LLM inference, which is poor, indicating limitations in memory-intensive or massive-scale AI workloads.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D16ads_v6 offers a balanced resource density, combining dedicated AMD EPYC compute power with a substantial local NVMe SSD. This makes it a cost-effective option for workloads requiring fast local scratch space without the premium cost of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated instances. It is well-suited for general-purpose applications, software compilation, web serving, text processing, and moderate database operations.
